t.2.80.1: Then Guha, who roamed the deep forest, described to the immeasurable Bharata the noble devotion of the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa.
t.2.80.2: To Lakṣmaṇa, who stayed wide awake for the protection of his brother, endowed with virtues and bearing an excellent bow and arrows, I spoke.
t.2.80.3: Dear one, this comfortable bed has been prepared for you. Take heart, O joy of the Rāghavas, and lie upon it in comfort.
t.2.80.4: All these people are accustomed to hardships, while you are accustomed to comfort; O righteous one, we will keep watch through the night to guard him.
t.2.80.5: For there is no one on earth dearer to me than Rāma. Do not be anxious; I say this before your very face, and would I speak an untruth to you?
t.2.80.6: Through his grace I hope to win very great fame in this world, abundant attainment of dharma, and the complete attainment of wealth.
t.2.80.7: Therefore I, bow in hand, together with all my kinsmen, shall guard my dear friend Rāma as he lies sleeping with Sītā.
t.2.80.8: For nothing in this forest is unknown to me, as I roam it always; indeed, we could withstand in battle even an army of four divisions.
t.2.80.9: When we had spoken to him thus, all of us were gently won over by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, who looked to dharma alone.
t.2.80.10: While Dāśarathi lies upon the ground together with Sītā, how can sleep be obtained by me, or life, or any pleasures?
t.2.80.11: Look, O Guha: he whom not even all the gods and asuras together could withstand in battle now lies upon the grass with Sītā.
t.2.80.12: Won through great austerity and through manifold toils, this is the one son of Daśaratha, bearing marks worthy of his father.
t.2.80.13: When he has been sent into exile, the king will not live long; surely the earth will very soon become a widow.
t.2.80.14: Having raised a very great wailing, the women have fallen silent from exhaustion; surely the king's palace is now hushed, its clamor stilled.
t.2.80.15: Kausalyā, and the king, and likewise my own mother: I do not expect that all of them will live through this night.
t.2.80.16: My own mother may indeed go on living, under the care of Śatrughna; but Kausalyā, mother of a hero, who is stricken with grief, will surely perish.
t.2.80.17: Without attaining his heart's desire, which has slipped past him again and again, and without installing Rāma in the kingdom, my father will perish.
t.2.80.18: For when that time has come, those whose purpose has been fulfilled will perform the last sacraments for their departed father, the lord of the earth, in all the rites due to the dead.
t.2.80.20: It was crowded with elephants, horses and chariots, resounding with the sound of musical instruments, filled with every kind of auspicious thing, and thronged with joyful, well-nourished people.
t.2.80.19: It was a city of charming squares and well-divided great highways, filled with mansions and palaces and adorned with every kind of jewel.
t.2.80.21: Happily they will wander through the royal city of my father, filled with pleasure groves and gardens and resplendent with assemblies and festivals.
t.2.80.22: May we, when this appointed term has run its course, happily enter the city together with him who is true to his vow, safe and well.
t.2.80.23: While that very great-souled prince stood lamenting thus, that night passed away.
t.2.80.24: At daybreak, when the sun shone clear, the two of them, having had their hair made into matted locks, were ferried across in comfort by me here at this bank of the Bhāgīrathī.
t.2.80.25: Wearing matted locks and clothed in garments of tree bark, those two mighty scorchers of foes, like leaders of elephant herds, bearing excellent arrows, bows and swords, went away together with Sītā, looking carefully about them.
